show_edit_result

focus_page_element

Retrieve paginated changes and validation problems for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use an operationId from an edit result to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it for proof or review.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

discover_workflow
Call this first, and again after conflicts. Returns a compact page of item IDs, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. Follow nextCursor for more IDs.

Call after discover_workflow. Set baseRevision to its exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Atomically applies up to 20 typed commands; updateNode patch.label accepts a string or a copied Snapshot label object. On conflict, follow recovery.

5. complete — "Complete" — end — {} — (x:800, y:180)

- edge-fetch-save: fetch-orders (success) → save-results (input)

discover_workflow
Call this first, and again after conflicts. Returns a compact page of item IDs, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. Follow nextCursor for more IDs.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow to inspect up to five current nodes or connections by stable application ID, including properties and relationships.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Set baseRevision to its exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Atomically applies up to 20 typed commands; updateNode patch.label accepts a string or a copied Snapshot label object. On conflict, follow recovery.
show_workflow_item
Use a current item ID from discover_workflow to select a workflow node or connection and bring it into view. For nodes, also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Focus a named page target or advanced CSS selector on the next browser focus or accessibility interaction. Prefer targetId values returned by discover_workflow; use selector only as an advanced fallback.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes and validation problems for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use an operationId from an edit result to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it for proof or review.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Set baseRevision to its exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Atomically applies up to 20 typed commands; updateNode patch.label accepts a string or a copied Snapshot label object. On conflict, follow recovery.

Use a current item ID from discover_workflow to select a workflow node or connection and bring it into view. For nodes, also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.

Retrieve application-authored completion evidence using an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use an operationId from an edit result to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it for proof or review.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Trajectory
Step 1
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, and again after conflicts. Returns a compact page of item IDs, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. Follow nextCursor for more IDs.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow to inspect up to five current nodes or connections by stable application ID, including properties and relationships.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Set baseRevision to its exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Atomically applies up to 20 typed commands; updateNode patch.label accepts a string or a copied Snapshot label object. On conflict, follow recovery.
show_workflow_item
Use a current item ID from discover_workflow to select a workflow node or connection and bring it into view. For nodes, also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Focus a named page target or advanced CSS selector on the next browser focus or accessibility interaction. Prefer targetId values returned by discover_workflow; use selector only as an advanced fallback.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes and validation problems for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use an operationId from an edit result to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it for proof or review.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Step 3
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, and again after conflicts. Returns a compact page of item IDs, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. Follow nextCursor for more IDs.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow to inspect up to five current nodes or connections by stable application ID, including properties and relationships.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Set baseRevision to its exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Atomically applies up to 20 typed commands; updateNode patch.label accepts a string or a copied Snapshot label object. On conflict, follow recovery.
show_workflow_item
Use a current item ID from discover_workflow to select a workflow node or connection and bring it into view. For nodes, also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Focus a named page target or advanced CSS selector on the next browser focus or accessibility interaction. Prefer targetId values returned by discover_workflow; use selector only as an advanced fallback.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes and validation problems for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use an operationId from an edit result to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it for proof or review.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Step 16
Thoughts:
I inspected the workflow and attempted to apply the requested changes, but the edit API kept rejecting the edit payloads with schema/validation errors. Summary of what I inspected and what I attempted, plus next steps.

What I inspected
- Nodes present: Start -> Fetch Orders -> Save Results -> Complete, plus an unreachable Alert Team action.
- Current edges:
  - start -> fetch-orders (edge-start-fetch)
  - fetch-orders -> save-results (edge-fetch-save)
  - save-results -> complete (edge-save-end)
- Alert Team exists (channel: Operations) but has no incoming connection (warning).

What you asked me to do
- Insert a Retry node after Fetch Orders with attempts = 3.
- Route Fetch Orders success -> Retry.
- Route Retry success -> Save Results.
- Route Retry failure -> Alert Team.
- Remove the direct edge Fetch Orders -> Save Results.
- Show the edit result.

What I tried
- I prepared an edit that deletes edge-fetch-save, creates a Retry node and three new edges, and sets the retry node attempts property to 3. Example logical command sequence I meant to send:
  1) delete edge edge-fetch-save
  2) create node "retry" of type retry at approx. position x:410,y:180 with label "Retry"
  3) set node property attempts = 3
  4) create edge edge-fetch-retry: fetch-orders.success -> retry.input
  5) create edge edge-retry-save: retry.success -> save-results.input
  6) create edge edge-retry-alert: retry.failure -> alert-team.input

What happened
- The edit_workflow API repeatedly returned INVALID_INPUT errors. The errors vary between attempts but indicate the command payload did not match the expected schema for the edit API. Examples of returned problems (representative):
  - "Invalid input: expected object, received undefined" for various command fields
  - "Unrecognized keys" (different key names rejected on different attempts)
  - Final call returned a generic INVALID_INPUT with no actionable specifics
- Because the server rejected the payloads, no edit was applied and there is no successful edit result to show.

Proposed next steps (choose one)
1) I can keep trying different command payload shapes until one matches the edit API's expected schema. This may take a few attempts; tell me to continue and I will iterate until the edit succeeds (I will report each attempt and error).
2) If you prefer, I can instead produce a precise JSON edit payload (the one I intend to send) for you to review/approve before I try again.
3) You can apply the change manually in the editor (delete edge-fetch-save, add Retry node attempts=3, connect as described). If you want exact node/edge IDs and positions to use, I can provide them.
4) If you have documentation or an example of the accepted edit_workflow command format, please share it and I will retry using that exact schema.

If you want me to try again now, I will continue iterating until the edit succeeds. Which option do you want?
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, and again after conflicts. Returns a compact page of item IDs, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. Follow nextCursor for more IDs.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow to inspect up to five current nodes or connections by stable application ID, including properties and relationships.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Set baseRevision to its exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Atomically applies up to 20 typed commands; updateNode patch.label accepts a string or a copied Snapshot label object. On conflict, follow recovery.
show_workflow_item
Use a current item ID from discover_workflow to select a workflow node or connection and bring it into view. For nodes, also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Focus a named page target or advanced CSS selector on the next browser focus or accessibility interaction. Prefer targetId values returned by discover_workflow; use selector only as an advanced fallback.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes and validation problems for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use an operationId from an edit result to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it for proof or review.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, and again after conflicts. Returns a compact page of item IDs, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. Follow nextCursor for more IDs.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow to inspect up to five current nodes or connections by stable application ID, including properties and relationships.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Set baseRevision to its exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Atomically applies up to 20 typed commands; updateNode patch.label accepts a string or a copied Snapshot label object. On conflict, follow recovery.
show_workflow_item
Use a current item ID from discover_workflow to select a workflow node or connection and bring it into view. For nodes, also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Focus a named page target or advanced CSS selector on the next browser focus or accessibility interaction. Prefer targetId values returned by discover_workflow; use selector only as an advanced fallback.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes and validation problems for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use an operationId from an edit result to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it for proof or review.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

edit_workflow

Use a current item ID from discover_workflow to select a workflow node or connection and bring it into view. For nodes, also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.

show_edit_result

undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Step 20
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, and again after conflicts. Returns a compact page of item IDs, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. Follow nextCursor for more IDs.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow to inspect up to five current nodes or connections by stable application ID, including properties and relationships.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Set baseRevision to its exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Atomically applies up to 20 typed commands; updateNode patch.label accepts a string or a copied Snapshot label object. On conflict, follow recovery.
show_workflow_item
Use a current item ID from discover_workflow to select a workflow node or connection and bring it into view. For nodes, also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Focus a named page target or advanced CSS selector on the next browser focus or accessibility interaction. Prefer targetId values returned by discover_workflow; use selector only as an advanced fallback.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes and validation problems for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use an operationId from an edit result to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it for proof or review.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Trajectory
Step 1
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, and again after conflicts. Returns a compact page of item IDs, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. Follow nextCursor for more IDs.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow to inspect up to five current nodes or connections by stable application ID, including properties and relationships.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Set baseRevision to its exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Atomically applies up to 20 typed commands; updateNode patch.label accepts a string or a copied Snapshot label object. On conflict, follow recovery.
show_workflow_item
Use a current item ID from discover_workflow to select a workflow node or connection and bring it into view. For nodes, also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Focus a named page target or advanced CSS selector on the next browser focus or accessibility interaction. Prefer targetId values returned by discover_workflow; use selector only as an advanced fallback.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes and validation problems for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use an operationId from an edit result to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it for proof or review.
undo_workflow_edit

  - save-results — Save Results — action (destination: Warehouse)
  - alert-team — Alert Team — action (channel: Operations) — currently unconnected
  - complete — Complete — end
- Edges
  - edge-start-fetch: start.next -> fetch-orders.input
  - edge-fetch-save: fetch-orders.success -> save-results.input
  - edge-save-end: save-results.success -> complete.input

What you asked me to do

Trajectory
Step 1
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, and again after conflicts. Returns a compact page of item IDs, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. Follow nextCursor for more IDs.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow to inspect up to five current nodes or connections by stable application ID, including properties and relationships.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Set baseRevision to its exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Atomically applies up to 20 typed commands; updateNode patch.label accepts a string or a copied Snapshot label object. On conflict, follow recovery.
show_workflow_item
Use a current item ID from discover_workflow to select a workflow node or connection and bring it into view. For nodes, also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Focus a named page target or advanced CSS selector on the next browser focus or accessibility interaction. Prefer targetId values returned by discover_workflow; use selector only as an advanced fallback.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes and validation problems for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use an operationId from an edit result to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it for proof or review.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow to inspect up to five current nodes or connections by stable application ID, including properties and relationships.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Set baseRevision to its exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Atomically applies up to 20 typed commands; updateNode patch.label accepts a string or a copied Snapshot label object. On conflict, follow recovery.
show_workflow_item
Use a current item ID from discover_workflow to select a workflow node or connection and bring it into view. For nodes, also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.

get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes and validation problems for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use an operationId from an edit result to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it for proof or review.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, and again after conflicts. Returns a compact page of item IDs, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. Follow nextCursor for more IDs.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow to inspect up to five current nodes or connections by stable application ID, including properties and relationships.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Set baseRevision to its exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Atomically applies up to 20 typed commands; updateNode patch.label accepts a string or a copied Snapshot label object. On conflict, follow recovery.
show_workflow_item
Use a current item ID from discover_workflow to select a workflow node or connection and bring it into view. For nodes, also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Focus a named page target or advanced CSS selector on the next browser focus or accessibility interaction. Prefer targetId values returned by discover_workflow; use selector only as an advanced fallback.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes and validation problems for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use an operationId from an edit result to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it for proof or review.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

discover_workflow
Call this first, and again after conflicts. Returns a compact page of item IDs, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. Follow nextCursor for more IDs.

edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Set baseRevision to its exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Atomically applies up to 20 typed commands; updateNode patch.label accepts a string or a copied Snapshot label object. On conflict, follow recovery.
show_workflow_item
Use a current item ID from discover_workflow to select a workflow node or connection and bring it into view. For nodes, also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.

get_edit_result

show_edit_result

undo_workflow_edit

Thoughts:
I inspected the workflow and prepared the requested change, but my attempts to apply it failed because the edit API kept returning schema/validation errors. I’ll summarize what I inspected, what I tried, the errors returned, and the next steps I suggest.

What I inspected
- Nodes (id — label — type — position):
  - start — Order received — start — (x:40,y:180)
  - fetch-orders — Fetch Orders — action — (x:280,y:180)
  - save-results — Save Results — action — (x:540,y:100)
  - alert-team — Alert Team — action — (x:540,y:300)
  - complete — (end)
- Edges (from the inspection relationships):
  - edge-start-fetch: start.next -> fetch-orders.input
  - edge-fetch-save: fetch-orders.success -> save-results.input
  - edge-save-end: save-results.success -> complete.input
- Validation warnings observed prior to edits:
  - Alert Team has no input connection and is unreachable from Start.

What I attempted to do (matching your request)
- Add a Retry node named "Retry Fetch Orders" (id: retry-fetch) of type retry with attempts = 3, placed between Fetch Orders and Save Results.
- Delete the existing edge fetch-orders.success -> save-results.input (edge-fetch-save).
- Create edges:
  - fetch-orders.success -> retry-fetch.input (edge-fetch-retry)
  - retry-fetch.success -> save-results.input (edge-retry-save)
  - retry-fetch.failure -> alert-team.input (edge-retry-alert)

What happened when I tried to apply the edits
- I repeatedly called the edit_workflow tool with the necessary commands (createNode, deleteEdge, createEdge, updateNode).
- The edit_workflow tool repeatedly returned INVALID_INPUT schema/validation errors. The exact errors varied between attempts; some runs returned unhelpful "input did not match the registered schema" with no details, others returned diagnostic paths such as:
  - commands[0].node.properties: invalid_type (expected record, received undefined)
  - commands[0].node.position: invalid_type (expected object, received undefined)
  - commands[0].node: unrecognized_keys when I included a propertyName field
- I tried multiple variants (createNode with/without properties, createNode then updateNode, different placements of properties) but the API kept rejecting the request. No edit succeeded, so there is no edit result to show.

Requested next step / options
1. I can retry making the edit now. To increase chances of success I can:
   - Use a different node id/position or
   - Split the change into smaller edits (e.g., first create the node, then in a separate edit connect edges).
   - Try different shapes of the createNode payload (I already tried several).
   If you want me to retry, tell me which approach you prefer (single atomic edit vs. two-step creation+connect), or confirm the node id/label/attempts and I’ll try again.

Trajectory
Step 1
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, and again after conflicts. Returns a compact page of item IDs, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. Follow nextCursor for more IDs.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow to inspect up to five current nodes or connections by stable application ID, including properties and relationships.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Set baseRevision to its exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Atomically applies up to 20 typed commands; updateNode patch.label accepts a string or a copied Snapshot label object. On conflict, follow recovery.
show_workflow_item
Use a current item ID from discover_workflow to select a workflow node or connection and bring it into view. For nodes, also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Focus a named page target or advanced CSS selector on the next browser focus or accessibility interaction. Prefer targetId values returned by discover_workflow; use selector only as an advanced fallback.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes and validation problems for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use an operationId from an edit result to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it for proof or review.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, and again after conflicts. Returns a compact page of item IDs, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. Follow nextCursor for more IDs.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow to inspect up to five current nodes or connections by stable application ID, including properties and relationships.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Set baseRevision to its exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Atomically applies up to 20 typed commands; updateNode patch.label accepts a string or a copied Snapshot label object. On conflict, follow recovery.
show_workflow_item
Use a current item ID from discover_workflow to select a workflow node or connection and bring it into view. For nodes, also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Focus a named page target or advanced CSS selector on the next browser focus or accessibility interaction. Prefer targetId values returned by discover_workflow; use selector only as an advanced fallback.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes and validation problems for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use an operationId from an edit result to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it for proof or review.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Call this first, and again after conflicts. Returns a compact page of item IDs, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. Follow nextCursor for more IDs.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow to inspect up to five current nodes or connections by stable application ID, including properties and relationships.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Set baseRevision to its exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Atomically applies up to 20 typed commands; updateNode patch.label accepts a string or a copied Snapshot label object. On conflict, follow recovery.
show_workflow_item
Use a current item ID from discover_workflow to select a workflow node or connection and bring it into view. For nodes, also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Focus a named page target or advanced CSS selector on the next browser focus or accessibility interaction. Prefer targetId values returned by discover_workflow; use selector only as an advanced fallback.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes and validation problems for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use an operationId from an edit result to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it for proof or review.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Use a current item ID from discover_workflow to select a workflow node or connection and bring it into view. For nodes, also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.

get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes and validation problems for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use an operationId from an edit result to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it for proof or review.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

discover_workflow
Call this first, and again after conflicts. Returns a compact page of item IDs, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. Follow nextCursor for more IDs.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow to inspect up to five current nodes or connections by stable application ID, including properties and relationships.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Set baseRevision to its exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Atomically applies up to 20 typed commands; updateNode patch.label accepts a string or a copied Snapshot label object. On conflict, follow recovery.
show_workflow_item
Use a current item ID from discover_workflow to select a workflow node or connection and bring it into view. For nodes, also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Focus a named page target or advanced CSS selector on the next browser focus or accessibility interaction. Prefer targetId values returned by discover_workflow; use selector only as an advanced fallback.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes and validation problems for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use an operationId from an edit result to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it for proof or review.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.
